Download the full Norwegian business register

Source: R/download.R
brreg_download.Rd

Download a complete extract of the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities (~1 million entities, ~150 MB gzipped). The bulk endpoint does not support server-side filtering — it always returns all entities. Use brreg_search() for filtered queries up to 10,000 results, or download the full register here and filter locally.

Usage

brreg_download(
  type = c("enheter", "underenheter", "roller"),
  refresh = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  type_output = c("tibble", "path")
)

Arguments

type

One of "enheter" (main entities, default, ~196 MB), "underenheter" (sub-entities / establishments, ~75 MB), or "roller" (all roles for all entities via /roller/totalbestand, ~131 MB). All three are gzipped JSON.

refresh

FALSE (default): use cached file if available. TRUE: force re-download. "auto": revalidate against the server and re-download only when the cached copy cannot be shown current. Any other value is an error.

cache

Logical. If TRUE (default), keep the downloaded file in the persistent cache directory; if FALSE, use a temporary file.

type_output

One of "tibble" (default) or "path" (returns the file path without parsing).

Value

Depends on type_output:

  • "tibble": A tibble with ~1 million rows. Column names mapped via field_dict; arrays of objects are list-columns of tibbles. For type = "roller", one row per role assignment with the columns of brreg_roles().

  • "path": Character file path to the gzipped download.

Backend routing

The brreg API has two data access paths with fundamentally different characteristics, following the cansim (Statistics Canada) pattern of separate functions for separate access patterns rather than the eurostat pattern of auto-routing within one function:

  • brreg_search(): JSON API with server-side filtering. Fast for small result sets, capped at 10,000. Interactive exploration.

  • brreg_download(): Bulk JSON. Always returns the full register. Appropriate for any analysis requiring more than 10,000 entities.

Results from both paths use the same column names and types via field_dict; only observed columns are emitted (see brreg_entity()). The bulk is the JSON variant of each endpoint, the same representation the single-entity lookups and the update feeds use, so historiskeNavn and paategninger arrive as the nested list-columns historiske_navn and annotations exactly as from brreg_entity(). BRREG's CSV variant is not read: it is the register's own flattening, with different separators and a presence flag in place of the annotation array.

Memory and time

The tibble of the full register is built in memory. The gzipped array is decoded in batches of complete objects and the batches are bound one column at a time, so the peak is the result plus the decoder's transient rather than a multiple of the result. Measured on the live register on 2026-11-02 (2 cores): enheter, 1,179,853 rows and 91 columns, 14.6 minutes, a 1.6 GB tibble, 4.0 GB peak resident memory; underenheter, 870,571 rows and 43 columns, 7.1 minutes, 0.9 GB, 2.0 GB peak; roller, 3,426,438 roles of 1,154,321 entities, 11.1 minutes, 0.7 GB, 2.3 GB peak with jsonlite (yyjsonr, when installed, decodes each batch faster). A machine with 8 GB holds one full enheter parse and not two at once. type_output = "path" costs nothing beyond the download, and parse_bulk_json(path, n_max = ) (internal) reads the head of the array without inflating the rest.

Caching

With cache = TRUE (default) the gzipped payload is stored in tools::R_user_dir("tidybrreg", "cache") together with a sidecar recording the server's ETag and Last-Modified validators, and a later call reuses it. refresh = TRUE forces a new download. refresh = "auto" sends a HEAD request and re-downloads when either validator differs from the sidecar; when the sidecar is missing or the server sends neither validator, nothing can prove the cache current, so it is re-downloaded. With cache = FALSE the payload goes to a temporary file that is deleted after parsing; with type_output = "path" that temporary path is returned and the caller owns it. The cache directory is created only by this function, never at load time.

Metadata of the most recent download (url, etag, last_modified as a UTC POSIXct, downloaded_at, path) is available as attr(result, "brreg_download") on tibble output.

Tidy shape

Every tibble the package returns is tidy in Wickham's sense: one observation per row, one variable per column, one observational unit per table. The register nests two kinds of array inside an entity. Arrays of strings (business_address, postal_address, location_address, purpose, activity) are the line fragments of one value and are joined with "\n", which no fragment contains, so strsplit(x, "\n") recovers the lines. Arrays of objects (historiske_navn, annotations, any array of objects the register adds) are observations of another unit and are nested as a list-column of tibbles, one row per element with snake_case columns, NULL for an entity without them; tidyr::unnest() expands them to their own table. An empty array is not an observation and emits no column. Nothing is serialized to JSON text.

See also

brreg_search() for filtered API queries, brreg_updates() for incremental changes since a given date.

Other tidybrreg entity functions: brreg_children(), brreg_entity(), brreg_konsern(), brreg_prokura(), brreg_regnskap(), brreg_roles(), brreg_roles_legal(), brreg_search(), brreg_signatur(), brreg_underenheter(), brreg_update_fields(), brreg_updates()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && curl::has_internet()
# \donttest{
# Download full register as tibble (~196 MB download, ~1M rows)
entities <- brreg_download()

# Just get the file path (no parsing)
path <- brreg_download(type_output = "path")

# Force refresh
entities <- brreg_download(refresh = TRUE)
# }
}
